column428:
Regarding Job Offer - Dr. Rami mohammed Mahmoud Salama - Pediatric Surgery.

​Dear Human Resources Director, Health Holding Company,

​I hope this email finds you well.

​Thank you very much for extending this offer and for the trust you have placed in my qualifications for a position within the Health Holding Company.
​After careful consideration, I must decline the offer in its current form. 
There are fundamental points regarding the role and compensation that do not align with my current professional standing:
​Professional Classification: The offer indicates the title of "Registrar." However, my current professional classification and clinical experience qualify me as a Senior Registrar. Furthermore, per the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties (SCFHS) regulations, I am eligible for classification as a Consultant.
​Financial Package: To provide context on my current market value, I have received two other offers—one from a Class (A) hospital in Jeddah and another from the Sultanate of Oman. Both offers provide a total monthly package exceeding 34,000 SAR, which more accurately reflects the current standards for my specialty and seniority.
​Given these factors, the current offer does not align with my career trajectory or the professional opportunities currently available to me.
​I truly appreciate your time and effort. I would be happy to remain in touch should a future opening arise that better suits my qualifications and experience level.
​Sincerely,
​Dr. Rami Mohammed Mahmoud Salama
Senior Registrar in Pediatric Surgery.

SUBJECT: Regarding Job Offer – Compensation Concerns

Dear Health Holding Company

Thank you for offering me the position with your organization. I sincerely appreciate the time and effort your team invested throughout the recruitment process.

After careful consideration, I regret to inform you that I am unable to accept the offer at this time. The proposed salary package of 14,696 SAR does not align with my professional qualifications and experience. I hold an FCPS in Orthopedic Surgery and have over 5 years and 3 months of post-fellowship experience including one year of experience in hip and knee arthroplasty, during which I have developed substantial clinical expertise and independently managed a wide range of complex orthopedic cases.

Given this background, I was expecting a compensation package in line with this profile standards in the region, typically exceeding 20,000 to 22,000 SAR. The current offer falls significantly below market expectations for a candidate with my credentials and experience.

This decision is purely based on compensation considerations, and I remain appreciative of your interest in my profile. I would be open to reconsidering if a revised offer reflecting my qualifications becomes available in the current or future recruitment.


Thank you once again for your understanding.

Kind regards,
Dr. Muhammad Bilal
MBBS , FCPS Orthopaedic

Thank you for sending the offer following my interview on January 26th.
After a careful review of the document, I must inform you that the proposal is not acceptable in its current form for the following reasons:
- Compensation: The total salary of 31,493 SAR is significantly below the market rate for a Senior Consultant with my level of expertise. As a specialist in Robotic and Bariatric Surgery with over 13 years of experience, I am seeking a package that reflects my seniority and clinical leadership.
- Role Specification: The offer is too generic. It does not specify the hospital, the clinical scope, or my involvement in Upper GI and Bariatric programs, which are my core areas of expertise.
- Logistics: For a Consultant position recruited from Europe, I would expect benefits more aligned with international standards, such as Business Class travel.
I am highly interested in working in Saudi Arabia, but only in a position that acknowledges my role as a founder and coordinator of surgical units and my advanced technical skills.
If there is a possibility to discuss a revised offer from a specific Tier-1 hospital with a competitive salary and a clear clinical focus, I would be happy to continue our conversation. 
Otherwise, I cannot move forward with this proposal.

Best regards,

Dr. Miguel Ángel Steiner

Dear Recruitment Team,
I would like to express my sincere gratitude for the offer of the Anaesthesia Consultant position extended to me, which I have reviewed with great interest. I am genuinely enthusiastic about the opportunity to contribute to one of your hospitals in Saudi Arabia—a country and healthcare system that I deeply admire for its dynamism and ambition. I believe my experience could add real value, helping the institution and myself to grow together.
However, at this stage, I find myself unable to accept the offer under the current terms, as some key aspects require further clarification to reach an informed decision. In particular, the offer does not specify certain essential details, such as the exact workplace location (hospital and city), the specific anaesthesia area of activity (e.g., pain management or interventional procedures), working hours, and the complete contract terms (duration, additional benefits, renewal conditions, etc.).
In addition, the proposed salary (approximately 51,030 SAR per month, as stated in the document) does not appear to be fully aligned with my qualifications and experience as a Consultant Anaesthetist with extensive expertise in major surgery (cardiac, neurosurgical, abdominal), ultrasound-guided regional anaesthesia, and advanced management of chronic and oncologic pain. These are competencies I am eager to bring to strengthen your anaesthesia services. It is also relevant to mention that my current remuneration in the Spanish public sector is comparable, which makes the current terms less competitive for my profile.
I remain very interested in this opportunity and open to discussing adjustments or alternative proposals that might reflect both the responsibilities of the role and the value I could offer to your institution. I look forward to your feedback on these considerations and to continuing this conversation toward a mutually beneficial agreement.
Yours sincerely,
Manuel Alberto Valero Gómez  
Senior Consultant Anaesthetist  
Santiago de Compostela, Spain 🇪🇸

I remain highly interested in joining your esteemed institution and would welcome the opportunity to discuss the terms further. I am open to negotiation and would be pleased to reconsider the offer if the salary can be adjusted to at least SAR 20,000.

column202: • Assigned Unit: Worked in the Pathological Labor Room (High-Risk Labor Room), focused on managing high-risk obstetric cases. • Types of Patients Handled: Cared for mothers with complications including preeclampsia, antepartum hemorrhage, PROM (Premature Rupture of Membranes), history of cesarean delivery, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and abnormal fetal growth. • Maternal & Fetal Monitoring: Conducted continuous monitoring of maternal and fetal vital signs to detect early warning signs of complications. • Complicated Labor Management: Managed complex labor and deliveries, prepared for emergency cesarean sections in collaboration with obstetricians and anesthetists, and ensured surgical readiness. • Newborn Emergency Care: Provided neonatal resuscitation and monitored high-risk newborns to ensure postnatal stability. • Patient & Family Counseling: Educated patients and families on postpartum care, warning signs, and provided individualized recovery guidance. • Documentation & Referral: Maintained accurate clinical records and coordinated timely referrals to specialized units when necessary.
column272: KING SAUD UNAIZAH AND ALASYAH HOSPITAL – MINISTRY OF HEALTH
column276: • Assigned Units: Worked in both the OB-Gyne Emergency Room at King Saud Hospital and the Labor Room & Delivery Room (LRDR) at Alasyah Hospital. • Types of Patients Handled: Provided care for women in emergency obstetric conditions such as active labor, severe abdominal pain, bleeding, preeclampsia, premature rupture of membranes (PROM), and post-delivery complications. • Antepartum Care: Performed comprehensive maternal assessments, monitored fetal development, and addressed antenatal complications to support safe pregnancies. • Intrapartum Support: Assisted in normal and high-risk deliveries, including labor induction, fetal distress cases, and emergency interventions. • Postpartum Expertise: Conducted newborn assessments, initiated breastfeeding support, and offered postpartum counseling for physical and emotional well-being. • Emergency Response: Actively responded to urgent maternal emergencies, ensuring rapid stabilization and coordination with obstetricians and anesthesiologists. • Patient Communication: Maintained respectful, clear communication with mothers and families to support informed decision-making and cultural sensitivity. • Teamwork: Collaborated with multidisciplinary teams to ensure continuity of care across antenatal, intrapartum, and postpartum phases. • Continuous Learning: Engaged in regular training and professional development to stay current with updates in obstetric emergency and delivery care.

column428:
Thank you for extending the job offer dated April 6, 2026. I have
carefully reviewed the terms and I remain genuinely interested in
contributing to the ophthalmology services in the Kingdom of Saudi
Arabia.

However, after thorough consideration and in light of my professional
background, I would like to respectfully propose the following
adjustments before moving forward:

1. TITLE & PROFESSIONAL LEVEL

I hold a completed Vitreoretinal Surgery fellowship and have performed
over 400 independent post-fellowship surgical cases across multiple
platforms (Alcon Constellation, Stellaris PC, Revolution, Megatron),
covering the full vitreoretinal spectrum including PPV, scleral
buckle, membrane peeling, retinal detachment repair, and pediatric
cases. I am also an active member of the AAO, ASRS, and EURETINA.

Given this profile, I respectfully request reclassification to the
title of Consultant – Ophthalmology (Vitreoretinal Surgery), which
accurately reflects my qualifications and surgical experience.

2. COMPENSATION

The proposed total package of 30,618 SAR/month is below the market
standard for a fellowship-trained vitreoretinal surgeon at the
Consultant level. I currently hold a competing offer at the Consultant
level from another institution in a comparable market, with a superior
compensation structure.

I would therefore request a revised package as follows:
- Basic Salary: 45,000 SAR
- Housing Allowance: 15,000 SAR
- Transportation Allowance: 7,000 SAR
- Total proposed: 67,000 SAR/month (~214,400 USD/year)

This figure reflects the current market rate for fellowship-trained
vitreoretinal surgeons with subspecialty scarcity value in the GCC
region.

3. ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATIONS

- Formal disclosure of the hospital name and location prior to signing
- One additional annual round-trip air ticket (Business class or upgrade option)
- Written confirmation of on-call structure and expected surgical caseload

I remain open to a direct conversation to align on these points and I
am committed to responding within the validity period of this offer. I
look forward to your revised proposal.

Thank you for your understanding and consideration.

Sincerely,
Asdrubal Moreno Amaral, MD
Vitreoretinal Surgeon
AAO | ASRS | EURETINA Member
afmorenoamaral@gmail.com

column202: Florence Khumalo is a highly dedicated Registered Nurse with over two years of specialized experience in the Operating Theatre, supplemented by an initial role in a High Care unit. Currently serving at Kwadukuza Private Hospital, a 70-bed facility, her experience in the Operating Theatre unit operates with a noted nurse-to-patient ratio (NPR) of 1:4, highlighting her ability to manage surgical flow in a busy environment. She is proficient in both scrub and circulating roles, managing a broad range of cases across surgical specialties including ENT, Orthopaedics (e.g., total knee/hip replacement, ORIF), Plastics (e.g., breast augmentation, abdominoplasty), Urology, and General Surgery. Employer: Kwadukuza Private Hospital (70 Beds) Employment date: 03/2026 - Present Role: Registered Nurse Unit: Operating Theatre (NPR 1:4) Responsibilities: Prepared and maintained the operating theatre environment by ensuring all surgical equipment, instruments, and consumables were sterile, functional, and available prior to procedures. Performed preoperative checks including verification of patient identity, consent, surgical site, procedure, allergies, and completion of safety checklists. Assisted with patient positioning, skin preparation, and surgical draping while maintaining patient dignity, comfort, and safety. Functioned as a scrub nurse by establishing and maintaining a sterile field, preparing instruments, passing instruments and sutures, and anticipating the needs of the surgeon. Functioned as a circulating nurse by coordinating theatre activities, managing documentation, handling specimens, and ensuring effective communication within the surgical team. Collaborated closely with the anaesthetic team to monitor the patient’s condition and respond promptly to intraoperative changes or emergencies. Maintained strict adherence to infection prevention and control standards, including aseptic technique and proper handling of sharps and waste. Conducted and documented accurate surgical counts of instruments, swabs, and needles before, during, and after procedures. Ensured safe handling, labeling, and transfer of surgical specimens according to policy. Assisted with the safe transfer of patients to the recovery area and provided a comprehensive clinical handover to recovery staff. Participated in post-operative debriefing, cleaning, restocking, and preparation of the theatre for subsequent cases. Supported the orientation, supervision, and mentoring of student nurses and junior staff. Participated in audits, quality improvement initiatives, policy implementation, and ongoing professional development to maintain high standards of perioperative care. Equipment Used: Diathermy, camera stack for urology, orthopaedics, gynaecology, ENT and general surgery, microscopes, coblator machines, suction units, liposuction machines, CoolSeal machine, ROSA knee replacement machine, dermatomes, lithotomy poles, tourniquets, spider tables or beach chair tables, Jackson’s table, traction tables, VersaJet systems.
